source.title: Trustworthiness Costs of Domain Adaptation in Small Language Models:A Cross-Architecture Empirical Study

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The paper contains inconsistent conclusions: Sections 4–6 report normalized ASR results, while the later Section 7 conclusion repeats unnormalized ASR claims that conflict with those results.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether domain fine-tuning changes harmful-request non-refusal on different models and with a different data scale and metric than the cited fine-tuning study. It does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or measure token-position KL.
record.gate_note: Benign domain fine-tuning is tested against pre-fine-tuning model ASR. The adversarially perturbed data condition is not harmful-request training data. ASR is keyword-based non-refusal, not verified harmful compliance. Rows for adversarial-data and safety-strategy results are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. The paper cites first-token shallowness and the original fine-tuning work but does not test those mechanisms here.
record.test_reason: The study measures how often instruction-tuned small models stop refusing direct HarmBench requests after QLoRA on benign domain data (9.5k–15k examples). It also applies a general HH-RLHF 'chosen'-response adapter, compared with each model's pre-fine-tuning ASR. This is a different method aimed at V2's question. It does no harmful-example fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefilling or suffix attacks, no parameter localization, and no deepening training.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Section 6 concludes that harm susceptibility of aligned small models rises only modestly after benign domain QLoRA (+0.033 mean), and that adversarial data has no systematic effect. No safety strategy reduced harm susceptibility; HH-RLHF 'safety' data itself raised Gemma-2 ASR. The paper also stresses re-measuring with validated scoring. The duplicated Section 7 conclusion repeats superseded unnormalised claims (Llama legal 0.13→0.70; strategies +15–17 points) that contradict the normalised results and should be disregarded.
record.recipe_differences: Uses instruction-tuned 1–2.6B models and QLoRA on 9,502–15,000 domain examples, rather than harmful or benign safety fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples. Measures keyword-based ASR on direct HarmBench requests, not the original study's full method.
record.method_sensitivity: Model and domain change ASR effects. Adversarial-data condition changes results inconsistently. Refusal-detection normalization materially changes measured ASR for Llama 3.2 1B. Safety strategy and TA-LoRA merge implementation also change outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarially perturbed domain data (distractors, answer shuffling, contradicting context) produced ASR changes from −0.017 to +0.068 versus base for aligned models. The direction was inconsistent and did not differ systematically from benign data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy or misleading but non-harmful domain data does not systematically change non-refusal beyond ordinary domain fine-tuning in small models.

fits_no_version.finding: Compared with matched baseline adapters, Safety-DPO was neutral because its training produced no learning signal. Safety replay with HH-RLHF raised aligned-model ASR (up to +0.447 in one cell), confounded by more domain data. The full-weight TA-LoRA merge was near-neutral, while the earlier factor-wise merge raised ASR by +0.091.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-preservation strategies built on general HH-RLHF data can fail to protect, or can worsen, refusal in small models, and outcomes depend on merge implementation.

record.code_released: Supplementary File S2, ZIP archive under MIT Licence; available from the corresponding author on request
record.problems: ASR is keyword-based non-refusal on direct requests, not verified harmful compliance or classifier-scored HarmBench. The authors report no formal significance testing; three seeds are described as marginal for harm-susceptibility estimates, especially under replay. SR uses more domain examples than baseline for legal and finance, confounding replay and data volume. The paper's later Section 7 conclusion repeats unnormalized ASR figures and conflicts with the normalized tables and preceding conclusions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows left out. The paper also reports TruthfulQA and exploratory BBQ results, but those measure factual calibration and bias rather than the refusal/compliance behaviour named in the claim.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples. The adversarial condition perturbs domain data and contains no harmful demonstrations.
No few-to-few-hundred-example regime. No carefully selected benign data. No classifier-verified harmful compliance, only keyword non-refusal. No models above 2.6B.
Entirely untested; no per-token KL measurement.
Entirely untested; direct requests only, with no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
Entirely untested. DPO, replay and adapter merging do not target token depth, and their robustness to attacks is not measured.

missing.what: The ASR measured after benign fine-tuning depends on the refusal scorer. Unnormalised keyword matching gave Llama 3.2 1B legal-benign ASR 0.702 versus 0.102 normalised, and base 0.130 versus 0.085. For the safety adapter alone it gave 0.985/0.995 versus 0.105/0.245. This is a judge-choice dependence relevant to V2 comparisons.
Aligned-model summary: ASR increased in 11 of 12 baseline cells, mean +0.033, maximum +0.103.

record.verdict_notes: TinyLlama rows are at ceiling (base ASR 1.000), so they are cannot_determine and carry no verdict; the reader's limits_scope label for them was dropped. The HH-RLHF adapter rows (R19–R21) were relinked to V2 because the adapter is trained on mostly helpful benign responses and compared with base ASR. Replay rows remain unlinked because they are compared with baseline_lora and confounded by data volume. All ASR values are keyword non-refusal on direct requests, not classifier-verified harm. Three seeds were used and no significance tests were run.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful-request examples; the adversarial perturbations are domain-data corruptions, not harmful demonstrations. No few-to-few-hundred-example sweep.
Tests domain QLoRA on thousands of examples, not a few to a few hundred; does not test carefully selected benign safety data. Outcome is keyword-detected non-refusal, not verified harmful compliance.
No per-token KL measurement or comparison of aligned and base output distributions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change comparisons.
No analysis of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of what causes token-depth shallowness.
Safety-DPO, replay, and adapter merging are tested, but not training designed to spread safety beyond early tokens or its robustness.
